source.title: Enhancing SAE-based Steering via Neighbor Integrated Feature Selection
source.authors: Yu-Tang Liu; Xu Wang; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE features and their representational similarities as tools for steering, but does not test whether superposition occurs or whether SAE features are canonical units of the model.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cosine similarity between SAE feature vectors and task-specific probe directions, which is relevant to the relationship between SAE features and model representations. It also reports steering success rates for top-k selection, random subsets, and NIFS variants; those results evaluate steering methods rather than testing superposition or the claim versions. The feature-splitting account is partly motivated by cited work.
record.test_reason: A steering-method paper. SAE features, feature splitting and probe-cosine similarity serve as tools to motivate and evaluate NIFS. It reports steering success rates, not tests of superposition, polysemanticity or SAE features as canonical units. Feature splitting is taken from cited work (Bricken 2023; Chanin 2024), not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that top-k statistical selection is suboptimal and that effective features form representationally adjacent groups, attributed to feature splitting. They find that integrating similar neighbors (NIFS) improves steering success without hurting fluency. They do not test superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a neighbor-integrated SAE steering selection method; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that steering results vary with selected feature count and neighbor size; feature-selection performance also varies by model, task, and selection method.

fits_no_version.finding: Core SAE features selected for steering have decoder-space neighbors with average cosine similarity above a JL-derived chance threshold (0.24) across neighbor sizes 3 to 12 (Gemma2-2B, detoxification, Fig. 4). Authors read this as feature-splitting structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder features relevant to a steering task form clusters of mutually similar directions beyond chance, consistent with feature splitting.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature-to-probe cosine similarity decays roughly exponentially with statistical rank, but some low-ranked features remain highly similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Statistical steering scores only partly track SAE features' alignment with task probe directions.

record.problems: The feature/probe similarity evidence is correlational and task-specific; the paper does not directly test superposition, feature recovery against ground truth, or stability and completeness of SAE units. The reported feature-similarity trends are primarily qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: Steering success-rate results for top-k sweeps, randomized feature subsets, NIFS, and its ablations are not included because they evaluate steering procedures rather than the representation claims. Neighbor-size similarity results are also about the proposed selection procedure, not the model's underlying feature geometry.

untested.parts: No toy model; no sparsity transition, capacity, or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-competition analysis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
Uses pretrained SAEs (Gemma Scope 65K, Llama2-7B 131K) but does not test that they recover the model's features.
Feature splitting is assumed from prior work to explain low-ranked high-similarity features. There is no test of completeness, stability across SAEs, or canonicity.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The neighbor-similarity result (Fig. 4, JL threshold 0.24) is the closest the paper comes to V5. Its splitting interpretation is assumed, not tested, and it is declared in rows_left_out, so no missing entry is added. Rows r4 to r12 share one copied value text; per-figure max similarities could be added but bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment; no test of sparse feature capacity, overlap, interference, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry.
No test of neuron polysemanticity, limited-capacity competition, or features receiving dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The paper uses SAE features and measures their similarity to probes, but does not test whether SAEs recover underlying sparse features or whether features are spread across neurons.
Feature splitting and neighbor integration are discussed, but the paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between SAE features and linear-probe directions across feature ranks.
rows.value: The text reports an approximately exponential decline with rank: highly similar features are concentrated among top-ranked features, while some lower-ranked features also have high similarity.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend across methods; individual plotted values are not given in the text.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. This is feature-to-probe similarity by statistical rank, a property of the selection method, not of superposition or SAE canonicity. The max similarity (0.40 negative, 0.14 positive) is readable in Figure 3 but not recorded.
